 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE M. R. MENGDEY
Date : 14/06/2024  ORAL ORDER 1.

By way of the present application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the applicant-accused has prayed for enlarging him on anticipatory bail in connection with the FIR being C.R. No. 11188009240293 of 2024 registered wit h Modasa Town Police Station, Arvalli, for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. Heard learned Advocate for the Applicant and learned APP for the Respondent - State.
3. Rule.
Learned APP waives service of notice of Rule on behalf of the Respondent - State.

4. Learned Advocate for the Applicant has submitted that the Applicant is apprehending his arrest in connection the aforesaid FIR and in this connection the earlier application filed by the Applicant before the learned NEUTRAL CITATION
ORDER DATED: 14/06/2024 Raj Pandya @ Raj Kaushikkumar Pandya vs State Of Gujarat on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148496656/

sentences.text: 1 undefined Sessions Court came to be dis-allowed.

5. Learned A P P appearing on behalf of the respondent - State has opposed grant of anticipatory bail contending that the applicant was very much part of the conspiracy which was hatched for commission of the offence in question.
As a part of the said conspiracy, the car belonging to the co- accused had been sold to the first informant for consideration of Rs.12 lakhs.
The amount of consideration had been collected by the present applicant.
Thus there is an active involvement of the present applicant in commission of the offence in question.
He therefore submitted that looking to the nature of offence the Application may be dismissed.
6. Heard learned Advocates for the parties and perused the record.
It is the case of the prosecution against the accused persons that the car belonging to the accused No.1, had been sold to the first informant for consideration of Rs.12 lakhs.
The said amount of consideration had been collected by the present applicant.

However, when the first informant went for registering his name as the owner of the said car, an objection was raised by the co-accused qua the said registration and therefore, the registration could not be done.
It is an admitted position that the present applicant is not the registered owner of the car in question.
Considering the aforesaid aspect and considering the nature of allegations levelled against the present Applicant, this Court is inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.

7. This Court has considered following aspects,
(a) as per catena of decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court there are mainly two factors which are required to be considered by this court;
 (i) prima facie case  (ii) requirement of accused for custodial interrogation.

This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre Vs. Further, by exercising the discretion under Section 438 Cr.P.C, the doors of remand by the Investigating Officer is open and therefore also this court is inclined to exercise powers under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
9.
In the result, the present application is allowed.
